headline: Load spike and building sleep debt say protect today — treat the tempo as optional, not a must-hit.
body_state: Readiness 48/100 (moderate), but today's overall verdict reads **red**, driven by sleep: only 6.3h last night, deep sleep just 11% (2520s of 22620s total) against a 13-23% restorative band, and 25h of accumulated 14-day sleep debt. Layered on that, acute:chronic load ratio is 1.83 ("high" — 2-4x injury risk territory) and monotony sits at 2.1, both overtraining precursors. HRV 48ms is balanced, resting HR 50 (up from 46 yesterday), body battery 46/100 after a modest overnight recharge (+48). No illness signal — skin temp only +0.2°C.
session: Plan calls for a 4km tempo (10min easy @ 4:50-5:19/km → 4km @ 4:18-4:32/km threshold → 10min easy) — a genuine quality day. Given the red load/sleep flag, don't chase the full prescription: run the warmup, then either hold tempo to 2-3km at the top of the pace band or drop it to a hard-effort-not-max cruise and bail early if HR won't settle under ~163 (LTHR). No second session is on today's calendar, so this is the only load risk today — protect tonight's sleep instead of pushing the run.
recent: Aug 11 stacked a hard Un1t class (RPE7, 53% time in Z4, no cooldown taper) with a 32km easy bike ride — the ride was properly easy (70%+ Z1-2), but total volume that day was high. Aug 10's "easy" treadmill run ran 89.7% in zone 3 at 4:27/km — the grey-zone pattern (only 17.8% true easy vs an 80% target) is still the #1 limiter. Cadence stayed at 157.6 spm, still well under the 168-172 target set two days ago.
focus: Respect the red flag today: trim or shorten the tempo rather than forcing the full 4km, and get to bed ~60min earlier tonight.
When a session is labeled easy, actually run it easy — HR 115-130, not 130-140s.
Keep building cadence toward 168-172 spm; still sitting at 157-163 across recent runs.
